messages.text:
Hello Sharon,
 

 Thank you for your interest on our products.
 

 The best choice for Minnesota is the Swamp Milkweed (Asclepias incarnata) , which is native to Minnesota and serves as an important host plant for the monarch butterfly. It is ideal if your planting site is moist, near a rain garden, a low-lying area, the edge of a ditch or pond, or on soil that doesn’t dry out too much.
 

 Common milkweed (Asclepias syriaca) could be a second choice if you have a large, sunny space and don’t mind it spreading.
 

 We’re here to help if you have any further questions
 

 Warmly,
 __
 Hari 
 

 Lasclay

messages.subject: Extra Seeds
messages.text: I had already received my 5 packs of seeds and I just received another 5 packs. I’m not sure if there was a mix up. Do I need to send them back to you?

messages.subject: Re: Extra Seeds
messages.text:
Hi Sharon,

First, thank you for flagging this instead of just keeping quiet — and I'm sorry it took us this long to come back to you.

There was no mix-up, and you don't need to send anything back. You ordered the 10-pack of Incarnata, and it reached you as two batches of five. Together they're exactly the order you paid for.

One thing worth knowing now that you have them: fall is the right time to sow milkweed. The seeds need a cold winter to break dormancy, so putting them in the ground this autumn will give your mom far better germination in spring than sowing them now.

Sorry again for the wait between your emails and this reply.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com

A quick note for transparency: this message was prepared with a new AI-assisted response system that we're currently fine-tuning. If anything is off, I can be reached directly at 581-982-5857 to sort it out quickly.
